data.exact_reserve_text: An overall improvement of GBP 5.0 million on prior years' provisions was experienced during the year. Improvements of GBP 0.9 million on motor, GBP 16.9 million on fire and other damage to property and GBP 2.2 million on pecuniary loss were partially offset by deteriorations of GBP 6.0 million on third party liability, GBP 2.5 million on energy, GBP 3.3 million on reinsurance acceptances and GBP 3.0 million on marine, aviation and transport.

prior_year_events.event_name: CG Restaurants & Bars v RSA / Stonegate v MS Amlin court rulings
prior_year_events.impact_description: new court case... expected to challenge the basis upon which claims have been paid to date, leading to a loss of 12.2% of capacity for 2018 YOA.

prior_year_events.event_name: COVID-19 / Australian High Court BI rulings
prior_year_events.impact_description: affected by COVID-19 and the associated business interruption ("BI") claims... particularly exposed to the decisions of the High Court in Australia, leading to current forecast loss range of (5%) to (20%).

named_events.loss_description: very severe winter storm and freeze, named Uri, hit the US state of Texas causing around US$15 billion of insured damage.
largest single loss event being Hurricane Ida, which hit the United States in August causing an estimated total insured loss of around US$36 billion.
extremely damaging flood hit central Europe in July which caused around US$13 billion of insured damage
terrible outbreak of tornadoes across the US Mid-West

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced an overall gross strengthening of GBP 18.7 million on prior year reserves, calculated from the gross claims development triangle. This strengthening was influenced by adverse development in several lines of business, including third party liability, energy, reinsurance acceptances, and marine, aviation and transport, partially offset by favourable development in motor, fire and other damage to property, and pecuniary loss. The 2018 year of account closed with a loss of 12.2% of capacity, impacted by new court cases related to business interruption claims. The 2019 year of account remains open due to ongoing uncertainties related to COVID-19 business interruption claims and Australian High Court rulings.
